title: Proverbs Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Proverbs 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Every wise woman buildeth her house
He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD
A faithful witness will not lie
The heart knoweth his own bitterness
questions.correctAnswer: Every wise woman buildeth her house
questions.explanation: The first verse in Proverbs 14 is 'Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.'

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:2 say about the one who walks in uprightness?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:2 states, 'He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD.'

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:3, what is in the mouth of the foolish?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:3 mentions, 'In the mouth of the foolish is a rod of pride.'

questions.question: What is said about the crib in Proverbs 14:4?
options: It is clean where no oxen are
It is a place of joy
questions.correctAnswer: It is clean where no oxen are
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:4 states, 'Where no oxen are, the crib is clean.'

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:5, what will a faithful witness not do?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:5 says, 'A faithful witness will not lie.'

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:6 say about a scorner?
options: He seeks wisdom and finds it not
questions.correctAnswer: He seeks wisdom and finds it not
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:6 states, 'A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not.'

questions.question: In Proverbs 14:7, what should you do when perceiving a foolish man?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:7 advises, 'Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge.'

questions.question: What does the wisdom of the prudent help him to do according to Proverbs 14:8?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:8 states, 'The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way.'

questions.question: What do fools make a mock at, as stated in Proverbs 14:9?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:9 mentions, 'Fools make a mock at sin.'

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:10, who knows his own bitterness?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:10 states, 'The heart knoweth his own bitterness.'

questions.question: What will happen to the house of the wicked according to Proverbs 14:11?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:11 states, 'The house of the wicked shall be overthrown.'

questions.question: Is there a way that seems right unto a man, according to Proverbs 14:12?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:12 states, 'There is a way which seemeth right unto a man.'

questions.question: Does Proverbs 14:3 mention pride in relation to the foolish?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:3 states, 'In the mouth of the foolish is a rod of pride.'

questions.question: Proverbs 14:6 states that a wise man seeks wisdom and finds it.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:6 states that 'A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not,' not a wise man.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:11, the tabernacle of the upright shall be destroyed.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:11 states, 'but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish,' not be destroyed.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is the end of mirth according to Proverbs 14:13?
questions.explanation: The end of mirth is heaviness, as stated in Proverbs 14:13.

questions.question: What will happen to the backslider in heart according to Proverbs 14:14?
options: He shall be filled with his own ways
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be filled with his own ways
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:14 states that the backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways, indicating the consequences of straying from righteousness.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:15 say the prudent man does?
questions.explanation: According to Proverbs 14:15, the prudent man looks well to his going, showing discernment in his actions.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:16, what does a wise man do?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:16 indicates that a wise man fears and departs from evil, demonstrating a clear distinction between wisdom and foolishness.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:17 say about a man who is soon angry?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:17 states that he that is soon angry dealeth foolishly, highlighting the consequences of quick temper.

questions.question: What do the simple inherit according to Proverbs 14:18?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:18 explains that the simple inherit folly, contrasting their lack of prudence with the prudent who are crowned with knowledge.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:19, who bows before the good?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:19 states that the evil bow before the good, indicating a reversal of roles in the moral order.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:20 say about the poor?
options: He is hated even of his own neighbour
questions.correctAnswer: He is hated even of his own neighbour
questions.explanation: According to Proverbs 14:20, the poor is hated even of his own neighbour, illustrating the harsh realities faced by the poor.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:21 state about mercy on the poor?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:21 mentions that he that hath mercy on the poor, happy is he, linking mercy with personal joy.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:22, what shall mercy and truth be to those who devise good?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:22 states that mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good, emphasizing the positive outcomes of good deeds.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:23 say about labor?
options: There is profit in all labor
questions.correctAnswer: There is profit in all labor
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:23 emphasizes that in all labor there is profit, reinforcing the value of work.

questions.question: What does the crown of the wise represent according to Proverbs 14:24?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:24 states that the crown of the wise is their riches, symbolizing the rewards of wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: A wise woman builds her house according to Proverbs 14:1.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:1 states that every wise woman buildeth her house, affirming the role of wisdom in building rather than destroying.

questions.question: True or False: The heart knoweth his own bitterness according to Proverbs 14:10.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:10 indicates that the heart knows his own bitterness, making the statement false if it implies otherwise.

questions.question: True or False: Fools make a mock at sin according to Proverbs 14:9.
questions.explanation: According to Proverbs 14:9, fools make a mock at sin, but the statement might be false if interpreted as them not doing so.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:25, what is the outcome of a true witness compared to a deceitful witness?
options: A true witness delivereth souls; a deceitful witness speaketh lies
A true witness speaks lies; a deceitful witness delivereth souls
Both true and deceitful witnesses deliver souls
Both true and deceitful witnesses speak lies
questions.correctAnswer: A true witness delivereth souls; a deceitful witness speaketh lies
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:25 explicitly states, "A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies." This contrasts truthful testimony with falsehood and their effects.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:26 associate with strong confidence and a place of refuge?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:26 states, "In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge." The fear of the LORD is the source of confidence and protection.

questions.question: How is the 'fear of the LORD' described in Proverbs 14:27?
options: A fountain of life to depart from the snares of death
questions.correctAnswer: A fountain of life to depart from the snares of death
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:27 describes the fear of the LORD as "a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death," indicating it brings vitality and safety.

questions.question: What contrast is drawn in Proverbs 14:28 regarding a multitude of people and a want of people?
options: The king's honour is in the multitude; destruction of the prince in want
The prince prospers in want; the king is dishonoured in multitude
Both king and prince prosper in multitude
Neither king nor prince benefit from people
questions.correctAnswer: The king's honour is in the multitude; destruction of the prince in want
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:28 says, "In the multitude of people is the king's honour: but in the want of people is the destruction of the prince," showing the importance of population for leadership.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 14:29, what characterizes a person who is slow to wrath?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:29 states, "He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly," associating patience with wisdom.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 14:31 say about those who oppress the poor versus those who honor God?
options: Oppressors reproach their Maker; those who honor Him have mercy on the poor
Oppressors are blessed; those who honor God lack mercy
Both oppressors and those who honor God have mercy
Neither oppressors nor those who honor God show mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Oppressors reproach their Maker; those who honor Him have mercy on the poor
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:31 states, "He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor," linking treatment of the poor to reverence for God.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'yārēʾ' (ירא) in Proverbs 14:26 primarily mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'yārēʾ' in Proverbs 14:26 means 'fear' or 'reverence,' specifically the respectful fear of the LORD which leads to confidence and refuge.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Proverbs 14:25, contrasting a true witness and a deceitful witness?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:25 uses antithesis by placing contrasting ideas of a true witness delivering souls and a deceitful witness speaking lies side by side.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of a 'true witness' delivering souls as found in Proverbs 14:25?
questions.explanation: John 8:32 states, "And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free," which echoes the deliverance associated with a true witness in Proverbs 14:25.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse complements the teaching of Proverbs 14:34 that 'Righteousness exalteth a nation'?
questions.explanation: Psalm 33:12 says, "Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD; and the people whom he hath chosen for his own inheritance," affirming righteousness as a nation's foundation.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Proverbs 14:25 in the chapter?
options: Proverbs 14:24 - The crown of the wise is their riches: but the foolishness of fools is folly
Proverbs 14:26 - In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence
Proverbs 14:23 - In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury
Proverbs 14:27 - The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life
questions.correctAnswer: Proverbs 14:24 - The crown of the wise is their riches: but the foolishness of fools is folly
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:24 directly precedes 14:25, as the chapter progresses in order; it discusses wisdom and folly in relation to riches and folly.

questions.question: What is the primary theme of Proverbs 14:29 and how does it relate to practical wisdom?
options: Foolishness is a sign of intelligence
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:29 teaches that being slow to wrath is a mark of great understanding, highlighting patience as practical wisdom.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 14:32 illustrate the contrasting fates of the wicked and the righteous at death?
options: The wicked is driven away in wickedness; the righteous has hope in death
Both the wicked and righteous perish without hope
The wicked are honored; the righteous are forgotten
The wicked have hope; the righteous are driven away
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked is driven away in wickedness; the righteous has hope in death
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:32 states, "The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death," contrasting their final outcomes.

questions.question: In the cultural context of Proverbs, what does the 'king's favour' signify as mentioned in Proverbs 14:35?
options: Approval and reward for wise servants
questions.correctAnswer: Approval and reward for wise servants
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:35 says, "The king's favour is toward a wise servant: but his wrath is against him that causeth shame," indicating royal approval is a reward.

questions.question: What is the literary significance of the parallelism found in Proverbs 14:30?
options: Contrasting a sound heart with envy using synonymous parallelism
Using metaphor to describe envy as rottenness
Employing chiasm to highlight envy and soundness
questions.correctAnswer: Using metaphor to describe envy as rottenness
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:30 uses metaphorical parallelism by contrasting 'a sound heart' as life with 'envy' likened to 'rottenness of the bones,' illustrating spiritual health versus decay.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 14:2 teach about human sin and the fear of God?
options: The upright fear the LORD, while the perverse despise Him
All men inherently fear God and walk uprightly
Sin is excused by ignorance in perverse ways
The righteous never fear the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The upright fear the LORD, while the perverse despise Him
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:2 states that he who walks uprightly fears the LORD, but the one who is perverse despises Him, teaching a clear distinction in attitude towards God based on moral behavior.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the consequences of speech does Proverbs 14:3 teach?
options: Foolish speech originates from pride and wise speech preserves life
All speech is equally valuable before God
Pride is justified when expressed openly
questions.correctAnswer: Foolish speech originates from pride and wise speech preserves life
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:3 contrasts the mouth of the foolish, which is a rod of pride, with the lips of the wise, which preserve them, emphasizing the doctrinal truth that speech reflects the heart and affects life.

questions.question: What doctrine about human understanding and folly is taught in Proverbs 14:6?
options: Scorners fail to find wisdom, but knowledge comes easily to the understanding
All who seek wisdom find it equally
Knowledge is only for the proud
Understanding is irrelevant to gaining wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Scorners fail to find wisdom, but knowledge comes easily to the understanding
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:6 teaches that a scorner seeks wisdom but does not find it, while knowledge is easy for those who understand, highlighting the doctrine that openness and humility are necessary for true knowledge.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 14:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:26 speaks of strong confidence and refuge for the children of those who fear the LORD, demonstrating God's covenant faithfulness to those who reverently obey Him.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Proverbs 14:27 by the fear of the LORD being described as a fountain of life?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:27 describes the fear of the LORD as a fountain of life, emphasizing God's life-giving grace that enables believers to depart from the snares of death.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 14:12 prepare for themes of judgment and salvation found later in Scripture?
options: It warns that the way that seems right to man leads to death, foreshadowing divine judgment
It promises that all paths lead to salvation
It teaches universalism by affirming all ways are acceptable
It denies the existence of any true way
questions.correctAnswer: It warns that the way that seems right to man leads to death, foreshadowing divine judgment
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:12 warns that there is a way that seems right to man but leads to death, preparing the biblical theme of judgment for sin and the necessity of salvation by God’s revealed truth.

questions.question: In what way does Proverbs 14:34 connect to the broader biblical narrative of nationhood and divine blessing?
options: Righteousness exalts a nation, while sin brings reproach, reflecting covenant blessings and curses
Nations prosper without regard to morality
Sin is unrelated to a nation's standing before God
Reproach is a sign of divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness exalts a nation, while sin brings reproach, reflecting covenant blessings and curses
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:34 teaches that righteousness elevates a nation whereas sin causes reproach, directly relating to the covenant theology of blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience found in the Old Testament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 14:5 and 14:25 teach about truth and testimony?
options: Faithful and true witnesses deliver justice, while false witnesses spread lies
Lying witnesses are excused if intent is good
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful and true witnesses deliver justice, while false witnesses spread lies
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:5 states that a faithful witness will not lie, and 14:25 shows that a true witness delivers souls, while deceitful witnesses speak lies, together teaching the doctrine of truthful testimony as essential to justice.

questions.question: What doctrine about human anger and wisdom is taught in Proverbs 14:17 and 14:29 combined?
options: He who is soon angry acts foolishly, but slow wrath indicates great understanding
Quick anger is a sign of wisdom
Hasty spirit and slow wrath are equally foolish
questions.correctAnswer: He who is soon angry acts foolishly, but slow wrath indicates great understanding
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:17 teaches that a man soon angry deals foolishly, and 14:29 says he who is slow to wrath is of great understanding, together showing the doctrine that controlling anger is a mark of wisdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 14:20 and 14:21 teach about social ethics and mercy?
options: Despising the poor is sin, but showing mercy brings happiness despite social rejection
Mercy on the poor is optional for the faithful
questions.correctAnswer: Despising the poor is sin, but showing mercy brings happiness despite social rejection
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:20 notes the poor is hated even of his neighbor, and 14:21 states despising one's neighbor is sin but mercy on the poor brings happiness, teaching the ethical doctrine of mercy transcending social bias.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Proverbs 14:12 teaches that any path a person chooses is acceptable. What does Proverbs 14:12 actually teach?
options: There is a way that seems right to a man, but it leads to death
All human ways lead to life
The end of every way is positive
questions.correctAnswer: There is a way that seems right to a man, but it leads to death
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:12 clearly warns that a way may appear right to man but ultimately leads to death, refuting the idea that all paths are acceptable.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 14:18 teach about the inheritance of wisdom and folly?
options: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent receive knowledge as a crown
Folly is inherited by the wise
Folly and wisdom are equally inherited
questions.correctAnswer: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent receive knowledge as a crown
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:18 teaches that simplicity leads to inheriting folly, whereas prudence leads to being crowned with knowledge, showing the doctrine of moral and spiritual inheritance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Proverbs 14:31 which connects honoring God with mercy towards the poor?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:31 connects honoring God with showing mercy to the poor, highlighting God's attribute of mercy as central to righteous living.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection is demonstrated in Proverbs 14:11 about the house of the wicked and the tabernacle of the upright?
options: The downfall of the wicked and flourishing of the righteous foreshadows eschatological judgment
Both wicked and righteous share the same fate
The wicked will inherit eternal life
The righteous will be destroyed with the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: The downfall of the wicked and flourishing of the righteous foreshadows eschatological judgment
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:11 contrasts the overthrow of the wicked with the flourishing of the upright, prefiguring the final divine judgment and reward themes in Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 14:22 and 14:23 teach about human labor and moral intent?
options: Devising good brings mercy and truth with profit, while evil plots lead to error and loss
Only talk, not labor, brings profit
questions.correctAnswer: Devising good brings mercy and truth with profit, while evil plots lead to error and loss
questions.explanation: Proverbs 14:22 states those who devise evil err, but mercy and truth belong to those who devise good; 14:23 adds that all labor brings profit, but talk leads to poverty, teaching the doctrine that moral intent combined with diligent work leads to blessing.
